questions.html:
Two fair six-sided dice are rolled simultaneously. Let the random variable $X$ denote the sum of the numbers appearing on the top faces of the two dice.

Which of the following correctly represents the probability distribution of $X$ ?
Let $x_k=k$ denote the possible values of $X$, and $p_k=P\left(X=x_k\right)$ denote the probability that the sum equals $x_k$.
questions.solution:
Answer: C

  2. $P(A \cup B)=P(A)+P(B)-P(A) P(B)$

Three candidates - $A, B$, and $C$ - are contesting an election. Exactly one of them will win.
Let:

  • $\Omega=\{A, B, C\}$ be the sample space,
     
  • $P(A), P(B)$, and $P(C)$ denote the probabilities that $\mathrm{A}, \mathrm{B}$, and C win, respectively.


You are given:

  • $P(A)=P(B)$,
  • $P(C)=\frac{1}{2} \cdot P(A)$
    (i.e., C is half as likely to win as A or B )


Let $E=\{A, C\}$.

Find: $P(E)$

  2. $P(A \cup B)=P(A)+P(B)$
